Run 167 was the manual backup vote at 2026-09-16T17:11:44Z (T-6.8h, k=5, expected $2,201.14, tx 0x4a5337976ba24006404e77b740e227be39c24caeda3ec4d2c0524c33c3c7e424). Run 170 is the binding executed allocation. Fourth consecutive epoch in which all three phases landed.
notes.headline: Realised $802.33, a new record and 1.17x the prior best of $685.17 ($0.4424 per 1k votes against $0.3778). Against run 170's send-time expectation of $748.01 that is +$54.32 (+7.3%); against its realized-at-boundary entitlement of $788.57 it is +$13.76 (+1.7%). Nothing went wrong this epoch: every one of the 16 reward tokens reconciled to the entitlement at a 1.00x amount ratio, so there were no missed claims and no mispriced gauge.
notes.token_reconciliation: All 16 tokens match on amount to within rounding (ratio 1.00x each). The +$13.76 over the boundary entitlement is entirely price drift between the vote-time snapshot (ts=1789602966) and the operator's claim-time marks, and it ran in our favour: BLOCKTRONICS 1.12x, wtFGI 1.06x, wtWEN 1.03x, wtPLBY 1.02x, chubal 1.01x, USDC/WETH/cbBTC/wtSPYM 1.00x, oHYDX 0.98x, fBOMB 0.98x. No token moved more than 12%. This is the first epoch since the AZUSD incident with no material price miss.
notes.price_staleness: Zero of the 161 tokens carrying boundary rewards had a token_prices row older than 24h at vote time. This is a clear improvement on the August state recorded in memory project_stale_price_misallocation (35 tokens then >24h stale) and means no allocation decision this epoch rested on a stale mark.
notes.null_symbol_defect: token_metadata holds a NULL symbol for 112 of its 229 rows, including 10 of the 16 tokens we were actually paid in (wtFGI, wtSPYM, BLOCKTRONICS, wtWEN, wtPLBY, wtNKE, wtGRND, wtMSTR, THEO, NOCK). The reconciliation in run_preboundary_analysis_pipeline.sh joins expected to actual by symbol, so each of these appeared twice - once as a 0x-prefixed address with a large negative delta, once as the operator symbol with an equal positive delta. The five largest 'deltas' printed by the review (wtFGI +$116.21 / 0x6aed8b1a -$107.51, BLOCKTRONICS +$72.55 / 0x7afe4384 -$56.71, wtSPYM +$40.14 / 0x31c2c141 -$39.79) are this artefact, not a real miss. Symbols and decimals were confirmed on-chain and are correct there; only the local cache is empty. Pricing is address-keyed and was unaffected. 71 NULL-symbol tokens carried $17,230.79 of the $61,734.65 boundary pot, so the labelling gap is wide enough to make the review unreadable every epoch until token_metadata is backfilled.
notes.reconciliation_denominator_defect: The token block of run_preboundary_analysis_pipeline.sh computes our share of each gauge as executed_votes / (boundary_votes + executed_votes), but boundary_gauge_values.votes_raw already includes our votes - the executed_realized block 40 lines above it subtracts them for exactly this reason. Our votes are therefore counted twice in the denominator and the expected side is understated. It reported token_expected_total_usd = $734.60 where the correct figure is $788.57, which is executed_realized_at_boundary_usd to the cent. The published token_actual_minus_expected_usd of +$67.73 should be +$13.76. The error scales with our share of each gauge, so it is worst on exactly the gauges we concentrate in.
notes.opportunity_gap: The review's headline gap of $127.62 (14.59%) is not reachable. boundary_opt k=50 = $874.52 includes $154.40 across six gauges on GAUGE_DENYLIST that the auto-voter is forbidden to vote, the two largest being 0x71354cf35384e8de09cad28d4ff4ef8acd6600ef ($86.47) and 0x8a6ca1a3b3f97562c804e5b85489aaa1f7bc8e27 ($60.58) - which are also the top two entries in the gap attribution. Re-running the same k-sweep with the denylist applied gives a reachable optimum of $834.86 at k=49 ($0.4603 per 1k votes). Against executed_realized_at_boundary of $788.57 the honest gap is $46.29 (5.5%), not $127.62. This is the same review/denylist mismatch recorded in memory project_denylist_review_mismatch; export_boundary_optimal_allocation.py still has no denylist flag.
notes.k_tolerance_cost: The largest controllable item in that $46.29 is the auto-k tolerance rule. Run 170's sweep peaked at $786.27 (k=50); --auto-top-k-return-tolerance-pct 5.0 selected the smallest k within 5%, which was k=14 at $748.01, giving up $38.26 (4.9%) of send-time expectation by design. Most of that is in the mid-range, not the tail: k=26 showed $778.80 and k=29 $783.92, so tightening the tolerance to 1% would have picked k=26 and captured $30.79 of the $38.26. The gas argument for a small k does not hold - AUTO_VOTE_GAS_LIMIT is applied as max(gas_limit, estimate x buffer), a floor rather than a cap, and at the 0.01 Gwei prevailing at send time the extra ~4M gas is about $0.10. The real cost of a higher k is downstream: claims run one tx per bribe contract (22 txs in 44s for 11 gauges last epoch), so k=26 roughly doubles the claim run and adds more dust tokens to Phase 4. Last epoch's swap slippage was only -0.66% across 8 legs, so that downstream cost looks small against $30, but it has not been measured on 1,000-vote dust positions.
notes.concentration: All 14 gauges we voted appear in the k=50 boundary optimum, so gauge selection was right and only the spread was wrong. Run 170 put 606,000 votes (33% of voting power) into 0xb11c863a49db1e72eeb3be0c12be87c2af32cc46, earning $236.03 at $0.3895 per 1k, while the unconstrained optimum left 1,000 votes there and redeployed the rest. Our own votes dilute our share, so the marginal return on a concentrated position falls below thinner gauges we skipped.

The epoch-1788998400 pot was claimed (claim_only_1788998400_20260910T095941Z.log, 22 of 22 claim batches successful) and swapped (swap_1788998400_20260910T100235Z.log, Phase 1-6 complete, 546.566364 USDC received on 8 legs) on 2026-09-10. notes.claim_swap_outcome: Claimed and swapped 2026-09-17. Gross received $802.19 against the $802.33 table - the $0.14 gap is a 1% transfer tax on fBOMB (826.891 sent, 818.622 arrived); the other 15 tokens landed at a 1.000 ratio. 13 legs swapped to 350.925865 USDC against $358.25 marked, -2.0% execution, the worst leg being wtFGI at -5.7% on the largest position ($109.57 for $116.21 marked). oHYDX (4,438.81, $86.36) and fBOMB (818.62, $13.53) are in HYDREX_SWAP_SKIP_TOKENS and were retained. End state: 695.077519 USDC in the signer, plus retained oHYDX and a running fBOMB balance of 1,847.258146. Total value captured $794.87, i.e. 0.91% of the pot lost to slippage and the fBOMB tax. Gas for the whole run was 0.000392 ETH (~$0.97). Claim txs: 38 escrow batches, all successful. Swap tx: 0x0e27f70e7c4dda3158365c99d78c22165ea7b06454bb27d9acb701d963382777.
notes.claim_source_defect: The first claim attempt silently claimed nothing and had to be redone. docs/OPERATIONS_RUNBOOK.md line 114 states that under VOTE_FROM=signer 'rewards accrue to the signer' and that claim_and_swap_rewards.py should default to --claim-source voter. That is wrong. Voting via delegation does not move reward accrual to the signer: veNFT 19435 is owned by the PartnerEscrow 0x768a675B8542F23C428C6672738E380176E7635C, the signer is neither owner nor approved (isApprovedOrOwner = false), and the bribe contracts book the entitlement against the tokenId - earned(19435, wtFGI) = 12.356981 exactly matches the operator table while earnedOwner(signer, ...) is zero for every token. The default --claim-source voter therefore called the address-based self-claim claimBribes(address[],address[][]) / claimFees(address[],address[][]), which resolve to Bribe.getRewardForAddress(msg.sender) and found nothing. Both txs returned status=1 having burned 510,681 and 510,559 gas and emitted ZERO logs (0xac19d9de7115bcfa11cba0eed873a82632095c40b07be46aa7d786f8d23d5077, 0xb3668595708b0b4b1daf8ed9ad6a7dce19aa9d20bd41b41245c2d23427a0d7d8). The run reported 'Phase 1-6 completed successfully' and 'Claim Batches: 2'. Nothing in the tooling would have told you the week's rewards had not moved. Re-running with --claim-source escrow --escrow-address 0x768a675B... claimed everything correctly in 38 batches. Until the default is fixed, pass --claim-source escrow explicitly and always verify token balances rather than trusting the success line.
notes.reclaim_guard_note: The already-claimed guard counts Phase 3 success rows and aborts, which is right, but it also blocks a --skip-claims swap-only run that touches no claim path at all. Both the corrective claim and the swap needed --force this epoch, which is exactly the flag you do not want operators reaching for by habit.
notes.recomputed_2026_09_17: Re-run after fixing the review pipeline. boundary_opt is now scored only over gauges the auto-voter may actually vote and comes out at $834.76 (was $874.52), so the gap against executed_realized_at_boundary is $46.18 rather than $85.95. The token reconciliation now reports token_expected_total_usd = $788.571050, exactly equal to executed_realized_at_boundary_usd, confirming the share-denominator fix, and returns 16 rows rather than 26 — the 10 phantom +/- pairs are gone now that token_metadata carries every symbol. The largest remaining deltas are genuine price drift: BLOCKTRONICS +$7.95 and wtFGI +$6.88. t1_pred/t1_realized also moved (k=38, $688.20 / $705.97) because the T-1 prediction is now denylist-filtered too, which it must be to be scored against a denylist-filtered boundary.
